questions.def: 'Were' implies hypothetical; thus, 'would' is the correct conditional consequence.
questions.question: Were he to refuse, we ___ find a replacement.

questions.def: 'Had' implies a past unreal conditional, requiring 'would have + past participle'.
questions.question: Had I known, I ___ differently.

questions.def: Past perfect 'had known' is used in the third conditional.
questions.question: Had I ___, I would have informed you sooner.

questions.def: 'Were it not' implies a past unreal conditional, needs 'would have'.
questions.question: Were it not for your help, I ___ failed.

questions.def: 'Only if' requires inversion of the auxiliary verb; hence, 'will'.
questions.question: Only if you apologize ___ I forgive you.

questions.def: Past perfect 'had arrived' is needed for the third conditional.
questions.question: Had he ___ earlier, he would have seen her.

questions.def: 'Should' implies a formal conditional; 'not hesitate' is the correct negation.
questions.question: Should you need assistance, please ___ hesitate to call.

questions.def: 'Had' sets up the third conditional; use 'would have + past participle'.
questions.question: Had they listened, they ___ the accident.

questions.def: 'Were' requires the base form 'be' in this construction.
questions.question: Were he to ___ here, he would disagree.

questions.def: 'But for' introduces a hypothetical situation; hence, 'would have'.
questions.question: But for your prompt action, the situation ___ worsened.

questions.def: 'Were' indicates a hypothetical situation, requiring 'would'.
questions.question: Were I in your shoes, I ___ accept the offer.

questions.def: Past participle 'informed' is used with 'had been' in the passive voice.
questions.question: Had we been ___, we would have acted sooner.

questions.def: 'Only then' requires subject-verb inversion, and 'did' fits the past context.
questions.question: Only then ___ I realize the gravity of the situation.

questions.def: 'Not until' requires inversion; auxiliary verb 'did' is appropriate here.
questions.question: Not until I saw it ___ I believe it.

questions.def: Past perfect 'had studied' is needed for the third conditional.
questions.question: Had he ___ harder, he would have passed.

questions.def: 'Were' in a conditional sentence requires 'would' in the main clause.
questions.question: Were it to rain, the match ___ be postponed.

questions.def: 'Had not' indicates a past unreal conditional, needing 'would have'.
questions.question: Had I not intervened, the situation ___ gotten worse.

questions.def: 'Only later' requires subject-verb inversion, and 'did know' fits the past tense.
questions.question: Only later ___ I ___ the truth.

questions.def: 'Were' implies hypothetical; 'would have' for past unreal condition.
questions.question: Were the circumstances different, I ___ agreed.

questions.def: 'Had it not been' is a past unreal conditional; use 'would have + past participle'.
questions.question: Had it not been for her, I ___.

questions.def: 'Were' requires the base form 'understand' after the infinitive marker 'to'.
questions.question: Were I to ___, I would act differently.

questions.def: 'Only by' requires subject-auxiliary inversion ('can' comes before 'you').
questions.question: Only by persevering ___ you achieve your goals.

questions.def: 'Had I known' signals a past unreal conditional, so 'would have acted'.
questions.question: Had I known the truth then, I ___.

questions.def: 'Were' + to-infinitive expresses an unlikely condition; 'would' is the main clause.
questions.question: Were he to refuse, ___.

questions.def: 'Had' + past participle implies a past unreal condition; 'would have' expresses result.
questions.question: Had I known, I ___ differently.

questions.def: 'Had' requires past participle for the conditional clause.
questions.question: Had they ___ about the delay, they would have been upset.

questions.def: 'Should' requires base form of verb in formal conditionals.
questions.question: Should it ___, the event will be cancelled.

questions.def: 'Were it not for' introduces an imaginary situation of lacking something.
questions.question: Were it not ___ your help, we'd be lost.

questions.def: 'Had' requires past participle form 'been' of the verb to be.
questions.question: Had it ___ for her quick thinking, the situation could have been worse.

questions.def: 'Even should' is a stronger, more formal version of 'even if'.
questions.question: ___ he apologize, I wouldn't forgive him.
